_note: Element cards (issue #24). Every 'measured' item must link to its evidence; every prediction must link to the record written before its test. 'where' is description, not measurement. Built into the table by table/build_cards.py.

Vb.sentence: A regular wobble in the pitch of a held note, about five to seven times a second.
where: Classical and operatic singing, on long notes
Violin, viola and cello: the finger rocks on the string
Guitar, with a bending finger or a tremolo arm
Synthesizer leads, with a slow oscillator on the pitch
place: Column: Periodicity. It asks what repeats, and how often, but of the pitch track rather than of the raw sound. That makes it a second-order element, built on Pitch (F0).
Row: Event (Z 10.7 to 13). One wobble takes 0.15 to 0.18 s: too slow to be heard as a pitch of its own, too fast to tap along to.

Expected, not yet measured: played about five times faster, a vibrato crosses 20 wobbles a second and stops sounding like a wobble. It becomes a roughness of the tone, in the Tone row. Played much slower, it becomes a slow drift of pitch.

listen.label: A held melody with a 5.5 Hz vibrato of ±40 cents. Switch it off to hear the same notes straight.

found.summary: We tracked the pitch of every held note, removed the note itself, and looked for a regular swing in what was left. Each one-second window was judged on its own, by the same gate for every recording.

chart.title: Vibrato rate found, median and 10–90% range

numbers: Every solo recording lands in the Event row: Z 12.29 to 12.50.
The piano without vibrato gave no false alarms; a 5.5 Hz vibrato written into it was found at 5.51 Hz.
Voices swing wider than the violin: ±30 to 40 cents against ±13.
limits: Inside a mix it is not solved yet: a violin with piano and a cello with orchestra gave no vibrato windows.
The Suno voices carry vibrato on only 11 to 16% of their held-note time, mostly late in long notes.

predictions.text: Vibrato lives in the Event row (Z 10.7 to 13).
predictions.fail: A natural vibrato read outside the row, slower than 4 or faster than 20 wobbles a second (the borders of the row).
predictions.evidence: Predicted by the second edition of the table before the measurement; measured at Z 12.29 to 12.50.

predictions.text: Generated singing starts its vibrato late in a long note, which makes it a fingerprint of generation.
predictions.fail: A human reference singer shows the same late start.
predictions.evidence: Seen in two Suno voices; no human reference recording yet.

predictions.text: Vibrato can be read inside a full mix, not only on a solo stem.
predictions.fail: No method finds it in a mix where it is known to be present.
predictions.evidence: Not found yet in the two mixes tried.
